cap: Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma arises by two roads. High-risk HPV in younger women produces HSIL with block-positive p16 and warty or basaloid carcinoma; lichen sclerosus in older women produces differentiated VIN with aberrant p53 and keratinizing carcinoma. Both spread first to the superficial inguinal nodes.
teach: The stains follow the biology. HPV E7 disables Rb, and the cell responds by overproducing p16, so p16 is diffuse and strong while p53 is intact (wild-type) even though E6 degrades it. On the HPV-independent road, a TP53 mutation drives the lesion, so p53 staining is aberrant and p16 is only patchy. Differentiated VIN shows atypia only in the basal layer, so it is easy to underdiagnose.
